summary: The refusal is now at the ENTRY. `pgraph_vk_image_blit()` returns at blit.c:498 under `image_blit->operation == NV09F_SET_OPERATION_BLEND_AND && bytes_per_pixel != 4`, which is 117 lines above the first destructive write and 236 above the first dirty mark. I CONFIRMED THE THREE LINE RELATIONSHIPS THE COMMIT CLAIMS, at the commit rather than from the message: guard return :498, `surf_dest->download_pending = false` :615 (`draw_dirty` :616, `upload_pending` :618, `pg->draw_time++` :619), `memory_region_set_client_dirty` :734 (VGA), :736 (NV2A_TEX), :744 (NV2A). The commit says the dirty marks are at :734-746; :744 is the third call's statement, whose arguments run to :745 and whose semicolon closes there, so the range is :734-745 and the claim is right to within the statement's own extent. THE LANE'S EXTRA HOIST IS SAFE, and I verified the reading rather than the conclusion. Nothing at all lies between the `bytes_per_pixel` switch and the guard: the switch's `default:` arm ends at :461 and the guard's comment opens at :463, so the two are adjacent and the claim 'nothing between the switch and the guard mutates surface or guest state' is vacuously true. The substantive question is what the EXTRA hoist skips relative to pass 1's proposed placement (immediately before the surf_dest block), and the answer is three classes and nothing else: (1) two asserts, `source_offset < source_dma_len` and `dest_offset < dest_dma_len`, whose only effect is an abort; (2) three VRAM download-if-dirty syncs -- `pgraph_vk_surface_download_if_dirty(surf_src)` plus `pgraph_vk_download_surfaces_in_range_if_dirty()` over the source and dest ranges; (3) three pure lookups, `nv_dma_map()`, `pgraph_vk_surface_get()` and `nv_clip_gpu_tile_blit()`, the last of which I read in full (nv2a.c:101-119) and which touches nothing but `d->pfb.regs`. THE SOURCE DOWNLOAD IS NEEDED BY NO PATH THAT STILL PROCEEDS, because no path proceeds -- the guard is a full return from the renderer op, and `pgraph_vk_surface_update(d, false, true, true)` at :434 is ABOVE the guard and still runs, so the bound colour/zeta flush is not skipped. Nor is the download needed by anything afterwards: all three syncs are lazy, keyed on dirty flags they clear themselves, and their documented purpose (the comment at :536-546, issue #7) is to order VRAM against THIS blit's own read and write. With no read and no write there is nothing to order, the overlapping surfaces stay marked dirty, and the next consumer performs the download. THE LEAF GUARD IS UNREACHABLE, NOT A SECOND SILENT POLICY: `bytes_per_pixel` is assigned only in the switch (:446, :449, :455) and never reassigned; `image_blit->operation` is never written anywhere in blit.c (only read, at :487, :627, :634, :648, :657); all four blit calls pass both verbatim, and `perform_blit_tiled()` forwards `bytes_per_pixel` unchanged (:385-386). So `operation == BLEND_AND` implies `bytes_per_pixel == 4` at every call, the leaf's `if (bytes_per_pixel != 4) return;` at :119-120 cannot be reached, and it is a bare `return` rather than an `assert` -- which is the right shape for a backstop and is NOT the pass-2 trap of an assert implied by its own condition, because nothing depends on it firing.
scenario: Pass 1's scenario can no longer occur. A guest binding LE_R5G6B5 or LE_Y8 with NV09F_SET_OPERATION_BLEND_AND and a full-surface rect now returns at :498, before `surf_dest` is even looked up, so `download_pending` and `draw_dirty` are never cleared, `upload_pending` is never set, `pg->draw_time` is not bumped, and none of the three `memory_region_set_client_dirty()` calls runs. There is no second route: `pgraph_vk_image_blit()` is the only function in vk/blit.c containing the surf_dest block, and it is reached only through `ops.image_blit` from pgraph.c:2110, behind `image_blit->width && image_blit->height`. The refusal is now indistinguishable from the blit never having been issued, which is what the finding asked for.
remediation: Effective, and the extra distance is an improvement rather than a risk. No action. Two residual differences from the cited precedent are recorded separately as N4 (opinion, no scenario) and the L2 residual under L2.

summary: Documented in the comment, code change declined with three reasons, and I ACCEPT THE DECLINE. The comment at blit.c:108-118 now names perform_blit_tiled() as the one site where `width * bytes_per_pixel != width_bytes`, which was the cheapest remediation pass 1 offered and completes the 'the clamp is authoritative' argument the fix rests on. I checked each of the three reasons for declining the code change and all three hold: width can only SHRINK there, because `chunk / bytes_per_pixel` truncates downward, so the outcome is a wrong picture inside the rect and never an extra byte touched; it is pre-existing, unchanged by either commit; and aligning `chunk` would alter the chunking of the TILED path for SRCCOPY as well as BLEND_AND, which BlitBeyondWidth is bit-exact on, with no arm on this fleet able to catch a regression there. I ALSO CHECKED THE CLAIM THAT ITS CHANGE 'STRICTLY REDUCES THAT SURFACE', because that is the kind of claim that quietly becomes 'and therefore fixed it'. It is true and it is not the stronger claim: Y8 and R5G6B5 can no longer reach the BLEND_AND branch at all, so the 4x and 2x cases are gone, but the 32bpp case pass 1 actually described is untouched -- `chunk = 16 - (offset % 16)` at :380 with a dest_offset that pgraph.c:2024 masks with 0x07FFFFFF and does not align, so `chunk % 4 != 0` is still reachable and `chunk / 4` still truncates while `done += chunk` still advances. The lane does not claim otherwise.
decision: ACCEPTED. Quoting the decline: 'Declining the code change: width can only SHRINK there, so it is a wrong picture and never an overrun; it is pre-existing and needs a valid GPU tile plus a blit that overruns it; and aligning chunk would alter the tiled BLEND_AND path that BlitBeyondWidth is bit-exact on, with no arm to catch it. My change strictly reduces its surface, since narrow formats no longer reach the branch at all.' I accept it. Bundling an unmeasurable change to a bit-exact path into a memory-safety fix is the wrong trade, and the documentation was the remediation pass 1 said it expected. The 32bpp residual stays open as pre-existing, and the comment is now where the next reader will find it.
scenario: Pre-existing and unchanged: an unaligned dest_offset plus a valid GPU tile plus a blit that overruns it (clipped_dest_size < dest_size at :558-559, dest_tile.valid at :626) gives a source that skews against the destination for the remainder of a tiled BLEND_AND row, and a leading chunk of 1, 2 or 3 bytes gives width == 0 and blends nothing. Wrong pixels inside the rect, never an overrun.
remediation: None required. If it is ever taken up, it wants its own arm with BlitBeyondWidth as the control, which is what the lane said.
evidence: Comment at blit.c:108-118 at f343580647. perform_blit_tiled() :365-388, chunk at :379-382, the call at :383-386 passing `chunk / bytes_per_pixel, 1, chunk`. pgraph.c:2024 `dest_offset = parameter & 0x07FFFFFF`. Tiled gating at :558-559 and :626.

summary: Both proposed remediations declined, and I ACCEPT BOTH DECLINES -- and one of them is more strongly justified than the lane argued. On the second proposal (gate the decline on `upload` so it mirrors GL): the lane says it would reintroduce #88's eviction through the download path, which is right, but the sharper fact is that the early return is REQUIRED on that path, not merely preferable. With upload == false and zeta_binding == NULL the Vulkan gate at :3213-3214 opens on the `!current_binding` disjunct alone, and the tail at :3536-3549 calls `download_surface_deferred(d, r->zeta_binding)`, whose first statement dereferences its argument (`if (!surface->draw_dirty || ...)`, surface.c:1362-1367). So without the return, the download path would have to bind something to survive -- which is exactly the create-zeta, evict-colour, copy-a-never-rendered-image behaviour #88 exists to remove. Gating on `upload` is not a smaller version of the fix; it is the defect. On the first proposal (clear draw_dirty and write_enabled_cache on the decline): accepted too. `pg->surface_zeta.draw_dirty` is pg-level state set by pgraph.c:2979 and draw.c:6991-6997 independently of whether a binding exists, and clearing it on a path that is not a draw would discard the record that a draw occurred. I also confirmed the cost framing. The lane's 'still cheaper than the two render-pass breaks the old policy paid' is correct: under the old policy both colour's and zeta's calls opened the gate, zeta evicting colour and colour evicting zeta back, two `pgraph_vk_ensure_not_in_render_pass()` per update; under the new one colour's gate is closed (current_binding non-NULL, and on the download path `upload` is false so the second disjunct cannot fire) and only zeta's call reaches it, one break per update. Pass 1's 'a per-update hash lookup' and the lane's 'one break instead of two' are the same cost described from the two ends.
decision: ACCEPTED, both. Quoting: 'Clearing draw_dirty would discard true pg-level state on a path that is not a draw; gating on upload would reintroduce #88's eviction through the download path. It accepts a hash lookup instead, arguing it is still cheaper than the two render-pass breaks per update the old policy paid.' Accepted, with the correction that the second is not a trade at all -- the return is load-bearing on the download path because the tail dereferences a NULL binding. Pass 1's own strong form remains unreachable for the reason pass 1 gave and I re-checked: download_surface_deferred() guards on the BINDING's draw_dirty and on download_generation == draw_generation (surface.c:1362-1372), so a draw_dirty accumulated while zeta had no image cannot make it download a surface zeta never drew into. No failure scenario behind either decline.
scenario: The surviving cost: while the overlap persists, `pg->surface_zeta.draw_dirty` and `write_enabled_cache` stay latched, so `pgraph_vk_surface_update()`'s zeta condition at :3604 is true on every non-upload update, `update_surface_part(d, false, false)` is re-entered, and it pays one `pgraph_vk_ensure_not_in_render_pass()`, one NULL-safe `unbind_surface()` and one `pgraph_vk_surface_get()` hash lookup to reach the same return. No wrong pixels. Recovery is intact: `!current_binding` reopens the gate on every zeta request, so zeta takes the surface on the first update after colour moves away, independently of buffer_dirty.
remediation: None. `write_enabled_cache` is a VMSTATE field (nv2a.c:1556) and I checked its readers -- surface.c:3600/3604 (the dispatch condition), surface.c:3547 (the clear), pgraph.c:2961/2979 (the accumulate). Leaving it latched affects the dispatch condition and nothing else, so a savestate carrying it true reproduces only the extra call.
evidence: Decline at surface.c:3289-3290 (`pg_surface->buffer_dirty = false; return;`) at 4726557b0f. Gate :3213-3214. Tail :3536-3549, the only site clearing write_enabled_cache (:3547) and draw_dirty (:3548), and OUTSIDE the gate's if/else so it normally runs on the miss path too. `download_surface_deferred()` :1362-1372, unconditional dereference on its first line, double guard on draw_dirty and generation. `unbind_surface()` :1828-1844, NULL-safe on both arms. Dispatch condition :3600-3606. Recovery interaction: the `color && r->zeta_binding && dims differ` reset at :3502-3505 is skipped while zeta is absent, which does not matter because `!current_binding` already forces the gate.

One VkImage' and `surface.c:3259` holds the NV2A_UNIMPLEMENTED; at f343580647 those lines hold the old one-line FIXME at :3227 and the NV2A_UNIMPLEMENTED at :3232, because the 59-line comment that shifts them arrives in the next commit. summary: M2's fix is carried in PROSE ONLY. The three-suite requirement lives in a sentence inside the `prediction` string ('THIS ARM MUST THEREFORE BE QUEUED AS A THREE-SUITE DISC -- --suites "Color zeta overlap,Color Zeta Disable,Null surface"'), and there is no machine-readable field binding the prediction to a disc. That is not a schema violation: across all 102 prediction files in the corpus, zero carry a `suites` key and exactly one carries `disc_id`, so prose is the established mechanism and the lane followed it. It is still the weakest possible carrier for the one fact that determines whether two of eleven legs are scored at all, and it is the same class of gap as the one pass 1 routed to lane.toolsmith.
scenario: A re-queue of either arm, done single-suite, silently re-creates M2 exactly. This is not hypothetical practice: rerunning before debugging a single-run score change is this project's own rule, so a rerun is the expected next action on either arm, and the person queueing it reads the request shape or the prediction's keys, not a paragraph in the middle of a 12,000-character string. request.sh's gate cannot catch it -- it builds `known` from $GOLDENS/<suite>/*.png (request.sh:299-305), so all eleven keys bind and it queues clean. The result would read PRE-REGISTERED with `Color_Zeta_Disable/MaskOff_ZB` and `Null_surface/XemuBug893` matching nothing, which are precisely the only two controls outside the subject suite.
remediation: Cheapest: add the three suite names as a top-level field in the prediction, or record `disc_id` the way one existing prediction does, so a re-queue can be checked against it by eye. The durable fix is the one pass 1 already routed: request.sh cross-checking the prediction's keys against the request's own --suites list, which it has at queue time. Neither holds the fold. Filed as LOW and not MEDIUM because the two arms that ran were queued correctly and the harm requires a future action.

summary: A CONSEQUENCE OF #88 THAT IS BROADER THAN 'WHICH ATTACHMENT IS BOUND', recorded because the prediction's falsifiers cover the depth TEST and not this. With zeta declining there is no zeta binding, and the depth/stencil clear is gated on one: draw.c:6774 `if (write_zeta && r->zeta_binding)` and draw.c:6870 `if (write_zeta && r->zeta_binding)`. So a guest clear of Z at an address colour holds now performs NO clear, where before the change zeta took the surface and the clear applied to it. That is the intended trade and the right one -- what it replaces is create-a-zeta-image, evict colour, copy a never-rendered image back over VRAM, which is the defect -- and for the one corpus configuration that exercises it the goldens adjudicate it directly, through ColorIntoZeta_ZB and ZetaIntoColor plus the seven must_not_move siblings. I am filing it as a SCOPE LIMIT rather than a defect claim, because I cannot name a title outside these three suites where it is wrong, and because the alternative behaviour is measurably worse.
scenario: A title that points colour and zeta at one address and then issues a depth clear expecting it to take effect gets no clear at all, and reads back whatever colour's image holds at those pixels. Inside Color_zeta_overlap this is measured by the arm. Outside the three-suite disc it is unmeasured, and the corpus contains no other suite pointing both units at one address, so nothing on this fleet can currently distinguish it.
remediation: None proposed and none wanted before the arm is judged. If the judged pair comes back clean, this is closed by the goldens for every case the corpus has. Worth naming in the #88 investigation record so the next reader of the overlap policy knows the clear is dropped and not merely redirected.
evidence: Clear gating at draw.c:6774-6790 and :6870-6884 at 4726557b0f, both `write_zeta && r->zeta_binding`. Every zeta_binding dereference in vk/ enumerated (`git grep -n zeta_binding` over hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/ at 4726557b0f, 60 hits) and all are NULL-guarded or behind `assert(r->color_binding || r->zeta_binding)`.

summary: AN OPINION, AND IT SAYS SO. The commit says the guard now sits at 'the same position solid_line uses'. It is one step later than that, and the step is not nothing: `pgraph_vk_solid_line()` puts its narrow-format return at :827, ABOVE its own `pgraph_vk_surface_update(d, false, true, true)` at :848, whereas `pgraph_vk_image_blit()`'s guard at :487 sits BELOW its surface_update at :434. So a refused narrow BLEND_AND still performs a full colour/zeta surface flush, and a refused narrow solid line does not. I could not turn this into a failure scenario and I do not think there is one: surface_update on the download path is a coherency flush that runs for every blit regardless of operation, advertises no write, and commits no bookkeeping to a write that will not happen -- which is the property M1 was about. It is also not freely movable, since the blit's asserts and its whole rationale assume the bound surfaces are current. Recorded so the difference is on the record rather than discovered later as a discrepancy with the precedent the commit cites.
scenario: None. Stated plainly because the audit loop says a finding with no failure scenario is an opinion and should be downgraded and labelled: this is one. The observable difference is a flush of the currently-bound colour and zeta surfaces that a refused narrow-format blend performs and a refused narrow-format line does not, and nothing in either path reads a value that flush produces.
remediation: None. If anything, one clause in the comment noting that the guard is below surface_update and why that is deliberate, which would stop the next reader re-deriving the comparison I just did.
evidence: blit.c at f343580647: `pgraph_vk_image_blit()` :419, frame-skip return :428-431, `pgraph_vk_surface_update(d, false, true, true)` :434, diag log :436-439, object_instance assert :441, switch :443-461, guard :487-498. `pgraph_vk_solid_line()` :775, frame-skip :782-786, SRCCOPY-only guard :789-798, switch :808-825, narrow-format guard :827-836, soft guards :843-846, surface_update :848.

summary: THE KHRONOS VALIDATION LAYER IS OWED, NOT COVERED, AND I COULD NOT RUN IT EITHER. AGENTS.md:845 makes it an obligation -- 'run it on any change to the Vulkan backend before calling the change verified', after it found eight defects in one afternoon that no capture showed (#34) -- and both commits are Vulkan backend changes, with #88 altering which framebuffer attachments exist, which is the class those eight came from. I TESTED THE BLOCKER RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT, and there are TWO independent blockers where the lane named one. First, the desktop build: /usr/include/curl/curl.h is absent, so the unconditional `dependency('libcurl')` cannot resolve, and build-linux/ has a configured meson tree with no build.ninja. Second, and not previously recorded anywhere I could find: THE LAYER ITSELF IS NOT INSTALLED ON THIS HOST. /usr/share/vulkan/explicit_layer.d contains only VkLayer_INTEL_nullhw.json and VkLayer_MESA_overlay.json; implicit_layer.d only VkLayer_MESA_device_select.json; /etc/vulkan/explicit_layer.d is empty; there is no ~/.local/share/vulkan or /usr/local/share/vulkan; VK_LAYER_PATH is unset; and a filesystem-wide search for VkLayer_khronos_validation* finds exactly one file, a Windows DLL inside Steam's CEF bundle on the mounted /mnt/c. So `[display.vulkan] validation_layers = true` would silently load nothing even if the build existed. Both fixes need a sudo password this session does not have.
scenario: No named failure scenario, which is why this is LOW and why I am calling it a coverage debt and not a defect. What it bounds: an attachment-configuration or pipeline-state error that produces no pixel difference would be invisible to every instrument available here, and no capture can substitute -- a validation error need not move a pixel. What I substituted, and it is reading rather than a run: every one of the 60 `zeta_binding` references in hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/ is NULL-guarded or sits behind `assert(r->color_binding || r->zeta_binding)`; `create_frame_buffer()` builds `attachments[]` with a running `attachment_count` that omits the absent binding (draw.c:1538-1546); `pDepthStencilState` is conditional on r->zeta_binding at draw.c:1761, :2561 and display.c:614; `get_optimal_zeta_load_op()` returns DONT_CARE with no binding (draw.c:2932-2935); and the zeta layout barrier in begin_render_pass() is behind a NULL check (draw.c:2962). The colour-only framebuffer #88 newly reaches in THIS situation is not a novel state -- any title binding colour without zeta reaches it constantly -- which is the strongest thing reading can establish and is still not the layer.
remediation: Record it as owed against #84 and #88, not as covered. Two owner actions, both one line: `sudo apt install libcurl4-openssl-dev` (already named in AGENTS.md:334) and `sudo apt install vulkan-validationlayers` (named at AGENTS.md:845 but never verified as present, which is worth correcting in the file). Then the layer belongs on the #88 change specifically, counting distinct VUIDs rather than lines. My recommendation is that this does NOT block the fold, for the reason above -- the attachment configuration is pre-existing and reached constantly -- and that it DOES block calling #88 verified.
evidence: AGENTS.md:322-336 (the desktop gap, verified 2026-09-14) and :845-850 (the layer obligation). /usr/include/curl/curl.h absent; `dpkg -l | grep libcurl4-openssl-dev` empty; build-linux/ has config-host.mak, meson-private and meson-logs but no build.ninja. Layer search: the five standard discovery directories listed above, VK_LAYER_PATH unset, and `find / -name 'VkLayer_khronos_validation*'` returning only '/mnt/c/Program Files (x86)/Steam/bin/cef/cef.win64/VkLayer_khronos_validation.dll'. What that instrument would have shown if the layer were present: a VkLayer_khronos_validation.json manifest in one of those directories plus a libVkLayer_khronos_validation.so, which is what `apt install vulkan-validationlayers` places. A layer installed under a non-standard prefix AND renamed would have been missed.
